item.content:encoded: It feels rather densely techno-babbley in some places, but I can appreciate a good hard science world-building dump like this. +1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Thought this was great. I'm a sucker for GOC para/militech and this is an excellent, narrative-driven example of the trope done well. The best part of this, imo, was the meat - the engagements are nice and removed but go into gory detail about the thing's achievements. It's written pretty well and it's got a lot of nice imagery - very little for me to dislike, here. Gladly upboated.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I mentioned the same thing regarding the SRAs, not just because it's a one-size-fits-all for 'reality-fixin' and is used all over the damn place, but also because it doesn't make sense (to me) for the GOC to use Foundation-engineered tech/nomenclature.

It's really all in the name though, I'd have much preferred something which is obviously the same thing, but with a designation that gives it more of an offensive feel. such as in the recent 1730 logs, where the MTF uses SRA grenades, which was the most badass thing ever.

item.content:encoded:
I quite enjoyed this. A slightly different perspective on GOC, with some depth and complexity. When all you have is a hammer, everything looks like a nail; when the problem IS a nail, a hammer is a useful tool.

The avian imagery and theme worked for me. Good use of multiple mythologies.
